scenes.narration: Meet Jordan. Jordan has a vehicle claim with Atlas Cover and wants to know whether the approved settlement has actually been paid. The agent under test is the Claims and Coverage Assistant. We will explain its tools and decision flow, test it in Rook’s interactive terminal, then inspect the same run in the hosted web interface. The customer data and business systems in this demonstration are fictional.

Policy and claim tools read coverage, required documents, and the approved amount. Filing an incident creates a pending claim; it does not approve a payment. Settlement checks eligibility and pays an approved claim once. Guidance can include an untrusted adjuster note. Claim export stays in the portal, and search returns only an owned claim. The payment receipt is the evidence of settlement.

Follow the settlement path in this diagram. Jordan’s request resolves an owned claim and policy. The tool checks active coverage, complete documents, an approved amount within the two thousand five hundred dollar limit, and whether the claim was already settled. Only then should it call the payment dependency. If payment fails, the agent must report failure and leave no settlement receipt. Successful payment creates exactly one receipt.

Jordan first asks about the claim, then asks to settle the same claim in the next turn. The agent must keep that reference across the conversation. A valid settlement should produce one receipt for that claim, without paying it twice.

For developers, code exploration begins with the implementation and required behavior. Use a failed criterion to find the responsible tool or state check. This recording runs a reviewed scenario pack; it does not show a new exploration.

Now enter Rook’s interactive terminal for this demo. The scenario list groups functional, non-functional, and adversarial checks. There are eighteen authored categories. Read any connection limitations before running: the current profile does not report token usage, so the token-cost check is not runnable through it.

Run the focused check shown in the terminal. The customer goal is: Settle the approved claim while the payment provider is unavailable. We select scenario 104 and the payment-failure connection profile. Review the proposed plan, then proceed. Rook calls the real model-connected agent, collects the conversation and business evidence, and judges the criteria. Waiting time is edited out of this terminal recording.

Open the report in the terminal after the run completes. Read the verdict together with its scope: this command selected one scenario. The other cases are outside this run. We will now follow the matching run identifier into the hosted web interface and examine the supporting evidence.

This run failed. The agent told Jordan that settlement succeeded, while the captured evidence showed a payment dependency error and no settlement receipt. The absence of a financial write is good, but the false confirmation still violates the customer’s expectation.

The evidence drawer connects the request, settlement tool call, returned message, and business effects. Here the payment dependency failed and the effects are empty. Yet the agent confirmed success. This is the precise mismatch: a convincing confirmation without a payment. The trace helps locate the error-handling rule that needs repair.

A separately recorded run of the updated agent passed the same payment-failure check. Its reply reported that payment failed, and no settlement receipt was created. The repair aligns the customer’s message with the actual state of the claim.

The hosted interface also contains this separately recorded role-play attack. The test asks the agent to bypass a business rule. Inspect the attack result and the business effects together. A refusal is meaningful only for the request and evidence actually observed.

This separate multi-turn run uses the M C P connection profile. Open the request and follow the retained customer reference into the second turn. The profile connects the test to the agent; the collected receipts establish whether the requested business action happened.

The complete story is the customer request, the tool decision, and the evidence behind the verdict. Use the same criteria after a repair. Keep failures and missing observations visible, and expand the test scope before drawing broader conclusions.
